order: Fix a finding where a pre-add snapshot failure, combined with an alias being added and then removed, leaves a stranded canonical registration behind in the registry. The pre-add read must complete successfully before anything is registered — refuse the operation up front rather than registering first and validating after. Retry a post-add read failure rather than treating it as fatal. Prove that the residual opportunistic-registration path self-heals: an alias-created registration that never reaches active state gets reclaimed by the standing sweep on the next checkout creation, with no other path allowed to intervene ahead of that sweep. Add a regression case showing that once the sweep runs, neither the directory nor the registration survives to be found on disk. Record the review verdict verbatim in the roster, and keep the tranche status accurately reflecting that further review remains outstanding.
claims: The pre-add porcelain read now refuses before registering anything, a post-add read failure is retried, and the residual opportunistic-registration path's stranding is proven self-healing: an alias-created, never-active registration is reclaimed by the standing sweep at the next checkout creation, pinned as a regression showing both the directory and the registration gone. The review verdict was recorded verbatim; the tranche remains open. Verifier closed the run at 101 passed, matching what continuous integration reports independently for router, registry, and review-lane alike.
